query: I am interested in high-entropy alloys for extreme temperature applications. How can we predict melting properties such as the melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for multi-component systems where experimental data is sparse or unreliable due to high melting points? I am looking for a hypothesis on a computational methodology that balances accuracy with the need to screen vast compositional spaces, along with prior evidence on why standard approaches struggle in this regime and what a valid boundary condition for such a method would be.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid computational framework combining Cluster Expansion (CE) with a Machine Learning (ML) surrogate trained on high-fidelity Density Functional Theory (DFT) data for short-range order (SRO) and a thermodynamic integration method based on the 'quasi-harmonic approximation with anharmonic corrections' will predict the melting temperature ($T_m$) and entropy of fusion ($	ext{S}_{	ext{fus}}$) of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with an error margin of <5% relative to experimental values, outperforming standard CALPHAD extrapolations in extreme temperature regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: A multi-principal element refractory alloy (e.g., NbMoTaW or W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20) in a disordered body-centered cubic (bcc) solid solution state at 0 K, with no prior experimental melting data available for the specific composition.
generation.intervention: Construct a Cluster Expansion model to capture the energetic landscape of local atomic configurations, train a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) or Neural Network potential on a sparse set of DFT-calculated energies and forces for various SRO states, and perform thermodynamic integration using molecular dynamics (MD) with the ML potential to simulate the solid-liquid coexistence or calculate the free energy difference between solid and liquid phases including anharmonic vibrational contributions.
generation.conditions: Temperatures ranging from 0 K up to the predicted melting point (typically >2000 K for refractory HEAs like NbMoTaW), pressures at 1 atm, and compositions within the quinary to quinary-equivalent space (5-7 elements).
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order (SRO) clusters and severe local lattice distortions characteristic of refractory elements, which significantly alter the vibrational density of states and the free energy barrier for melting.
generation.mechanism: Standard CALPHAD models rely on extrapolated binary/ternary parameters which fail to capture the complex, non-linear interactions and strong local chemical ordering in HEAs [PMC8282813::chunk::003::discussion::b590527e4b]. The proposed method uses the ML potential to accurately model the anharmonic phonon spectrum and the configurational entropy of the liquid phase, which is often overestimated in harmonic approximations. The CE model ensures the configurational space is sampled efficiently, while the ML potential provides the necessary accuracy for the high-energy liquid state without the computational cost of ab initio MD for the entire phase space.
generation.predicted_outcome: The hybrid CE-ML-thermodynamic integration method will yield a melting temperature prediction within 5% of the true value (if known) and correctly predict the trend of $	ext{S}_{	ext{fus}}$ increasing with compositional complexity due to enhanced vibrational anharmonicity, whereas standard CALPHAD will show deviations >15% and fail to capture the non-linear dependence of $T_m$ on composition.
generation.baseline: Standard CALPHAD (Thermodynamic Database) extrapolation using the Miedema model or simple regular solution models for the liquid phase, often assuming ideal mixing or simple binary interactions [PMC8282813::chunk::003::discussion::b590527e4b].
generation.boundary: The method is valid for substitutional solid solution RHEAs where the liquid phase remains disordered; it may fail for systems with strong intermetallic compound formation that dominates the phase diagram or for systems where the liquid phase exhibits significant short-range ordering not captured by the training set of the ML potential.
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy depends heavily on the diversity of the DFT training set used to construct the ML potential; if the training set lacks configurations representative of the high-temperature liquid state or specific SRO motifs, the prediction may drift. Additionally, the assumption that the liquid phase can be adequately modeled by a classical potential derived from DFT data at 0 K/300 K may introduce errors in the anharmonic regime, particularly for refractory elements with high melting points (>2000 K) where anharmonicity is extreme.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a specific refractory HEA composition (e.g., NbMoTaW or W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20) with a known experimental melting point (if available in literature pre-2024) or a composition where the melting point is known to be anomalous. Perform the proposed hybrid CE-ML-thermodynamic integration simulation. Simultaneously, perform a high-precision differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) or laser heating experiment on the same composition to determine the experimental $T_m$ and $	ext{S}_{	ext{fus}}$.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the absolute error in the predicted $T_m$ exceeds 5% of the experimental value OR if the predicted trend of $	ext{S}_{	ext{fus}}$ vs. composition contradicts the experimental trend (e.g., predicting a decrease when experiment shows an increase) for at least two distinct refractory HEA compositions.

cited_evidence.text: High entropy alloys and related compositions are a relatively young concept for designing alloys. The formation of such multi component alloys was reported independently by Cantor et al. [ [1] ] and the research group around J.-W. Yeh in 2004 [ [2] , [3] , [4] ]. In contrast to most conventional alloys, high entropy alloys do not possess a single main alloying element but comprise a composition of multiple principal elements. The exact definition of high entropy alloys varies from source to source. The most common definition includes alloys consisting of at least five elements with a concentration between 5% and 35% each [ [5] ]. Other definitions demand a configurational entropy of at least 1.5 R [ [6] ]. However, both definitions are overlapping in large parts. Additionally, further criterions like the formation of a single phase solid solution were suggested [ [7] ]. These definitions are discussed extensively in recent review papers [ [7] ] and books [ [6] , [8] ]. The focus of the present work lies on the alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 , which is considered a high entropy alloy in agreement with all these criterions. The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

The computational software could significantly affect the efficiency of HTC since massive calculations are carried out. In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. Metallic alloys containing multiple principal alloying elements, which are known as high-entropy alloys (HEAs) [1] – [3] , have attracted extensive research interest in recent years with many studies focused on their microstructure, mechanical properties, and underlying deformation mechanisms [4] – [6] . For example, as a new class of structural materials, certain face-centered cubic ( fcc ) alloys, in particular CrCoNi-based HEAs, have been shown to possess improved strength and exceptional damage tolerance, especially at cryogenic temperatures [7] , [8] .

A second prominent class of HEA systems are refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), which comprise mostly refractory elements and invariably crystallize as body-centered cubic ( bcc ) solid solutions; these alloys have been considered as promising candidate materials for elevated-temperature applications due to their exceptional resistance to softening and extremely high melting points [9] – [11] .
